notes: Shapes of the live-session artefacts stored on the Radicle branch ActiveDimensions/<DimensionName>/ and in each client's local store. These are NOT paper rules; they are the runtime contracts the Godot (.NET) client reads/writes. They are versioned like everything else so the community can evolve them. A concrete filled-in example lives in examples/ActiveDimensions/.

versions.notes: One per Dimension. Written at open_dimension, updated by any pusher; conflicts resolve to the higher turn.

shape.dimension_name: string (human label; also the branch path segment)
shape.rules_snapshot_commit: git commit hash of data/ frozen for this session (index.json notes)
shape.game_mode: mode_* id from game_modes.json (mode_mmorpg by default)

tileset.map_seed: hex; all hidden placement derives from it

doors: DoorId strings; one file each under doors/
shape.description: free text that pushers may change (in-game changeable descriptions)

logic.description: Governs the shape of ActiveDimensions/<DimensionName>/dimension.json, the one-per-Dimension descriptor written at open_dimension and updated by any pusher; conflicts resolve to the higher turn.max_seen. Required identity: dimension_id, dimension_name, radicle_repo, rules_snapshot_commit, game_mode (mode_mmorpg default), owners, tileset {initial_size, bounds, map_seed, extended_blocks}, turn, doors, last_push. The runtime deviates: peer.mjs buildDoor writes a deterministic dimension.json with radicle_branch, clock {rounds_per_turn, round_seconds}, layout, join hints and tileset.coordinates / reveal_radius / tiles_known, but WITHOUT created_at, owners, turn, doors, last_push or rules_snapshot_commit; bounds are axial q,r exposed as x,y and extended_blocks are discs ('disc r=10') keyed by the revealing peer. Context assumed: doc = the document under test, me.id, interval_index, ours / theirs documents for a merge.

prerequisites.description: dimension_id, dimension_name and radicle_repo are non-empty strings; radicle_repo is a rad: id.
rules_snapshot_commit pins the data/ commit the session plays with (peer.mjs omits it).
game_mode is a mode_* id from game_modes.json.
At least one opening player owns the Dimension.
tileset has a map_seed string and bounds with min <= max on both axes.
turn.max_seen is a non-negative number and doors is an array.

effects.description: Where the document lives: ActiveDimensions/<DimensionName>/dimension.json.
Conflict rule: the higher turn.max_seen wins.
Whether I am one of the opening players (may vote to migrate the snapshot).
game_mode or the default mode_mmorpg.
Bounds width (max_x - min_x + 1).
Blocks added by join_new_location (peer.mjs: reveal discs).
Doors listed in the descriptor (one file each under doors/).

validation.description: The descriptor shape keeps exactly the canonical key set.
dimension_id, dimension_name, radicle_repo, rules_snapshot_commit, tileset, turn and doors are the fields every reader depends on.
tileset keeps map_seed, bounds and extended_blocks; bounds keeps the four edges.
turn.max_seen stays (the merge rule depends on it).

entries.name: doors/<DoorId>.json (one per connected hashgraph part / clan entry point)

versions.notes: A DoorId is a magnet-style identifier for a hashgraph head plus the peers holding it. Joiners read this file, connect to the peers, and adopt the part. Many DoorIds per Dimension are expected until clans meet and merge.

shape.door_id: string (short id; also the file name)
shape.label: string shown in the join list (clan name, friend name, 'new frontier')
shape.hashgraph_head: sha256 of the latest finalized event in this part
shape.genesis_or_root: sha256 of evt_genesis or the evt_map_extend this part is rooted at
shape.turn: int (this part's turn at last push)
shape.pending_votes: int (governance votes gossiped but not yet batched to proposals/*)

logic.description: Governs the shape of doors/<DoorId>.json, one per connected hashgraph part: door_id, magnet_id, label, status (active | stale | merged_into:<DoorId> | closed), hashgraph_head, genesis_or_root, turn, members [{peer_id, character_id, class_id, tile, clan, last_seen}], region {center, strong_radius_tiles, reach_tiles}, map_summary, last_push {interval_index, peer_id, at, commit}, pending_votes. The runtime deviates: peer.mjs writes door_version 2 with door_id = peer_id (one Door per PEER in its own Radicle namespace) carrying peer_id, name, alliance, character_id / creature_id, tile {q,r}, life, life_max, hashgraph_head, clock {turn, round, action, phase, phase_ends_at}, known_members, known_tiles, map {seed, reveal_radius, blocks}, network {nostr, libp2p, gun}, radicle {repo, namespace, branch} and pushed_at; there is no magnet_id, label, status, genesis_or_root, region, map_summary, last_push or pending_votes. Context assumed: doc, me.id, interval_index, member tiles as {q,r} (hex_distance reads q/r; the paper shape says x,y).

prerequisites.description: door_id and hashgraph_head are strings; magnet_id is a magnet URI.
status is active, stale, merged_into:<DoorId> or closed.
turn is a non-negative number and members is an array.
region.strong_radius_tiles is at least 1 and no larger than reach_tiles.
last_push.interval_index is a number (needed to tell a stale Door).

effects.description: doors/<DoorId>.json under the Dimension branch.
sync_join_flow.join_new_location: the Door is stale when its last push predates the current interval.
Peers holding this part.
Members within region.strong_radius_tiles of region.center (tiles read as q,r).
Whether I hold this DoorId (and may be elected its pusher).
map_summary.tiles_revealed (peer.mjs: map.tiles_known).
Total life left on awake creatures in the summary.

validation.description: The Door shape keeps exactly the canonical key set.
door_id, hashgraph_head, turn, members and last_push are what a joiner needs.
status still names active, stale, merged_into and closed.
A member entry keeps peer_id and tile; region keeps strong_radius_tiles and reach_tiles.

versions.notes: What the Godot client holds in memory/on disk for the part of the hashgraph it owns. The hand is private; only its commitment is ever gossiped.

logic.description: Governs what a client keeps locally and never pushes as-is: peer_id, dimension_id, door_ids_held, hashgraph {events, head, finalized_turn}, character {ids, tile, stats, life_tokens = round(sum(stats)/10), element_tokens, combo}, cards {hand (max 5), deck_order_commitment, discard, archive, permanents_in_play}, known_map, region_peers {strong, reachable, far_known_doors}, pending_disturbances. The hand is private; only its commitment is gossiped. The runtime deviates: peer.mjs keeps entity {tile q/r, life, lifeMax, stats, permanents, tokens, elemPen, shieldElems, disables}, hand / deck / discard arrays, hg {tape, head, selfParent, otherParent, action, turn, round}, knownTiles + dimMap and peersPublic; it holds a single DOOR_ID (no door_ids_held), stores no deck_order_commitment (the digest is emitted in evt_join only), has no pending_disturbances, and persists the tape to game/sessions/<dim>/hashgraph.jsonl; its public snapshot (published every envelope) carries tile, life, permanents and tokens but never the hand. Context assumed: doc, outgoing (the snapshot about to be published), doc.cards.deck_size (runtime-supplied deck length).

prerequisites.description: peer_id and dimension_id are strings; hashgraph.head is a string.
The four stats are numbers (rule_14 Part B).
rule_10: the hand holds at most 5 cards.
The outgoing public snapshot carries no hand, deck or discard — only their commitment.

effects.description: rule_14 Part B: life = round_half_up(sum(stats) / 10).
rule_10: cards needed to refill the hand to 5 at turn end.
rule_11: archiving is allowed while deck + discard + hand stays at least 15 afterwards (deck_size supplied by the runtime).
Members of my strong region as held locally (peer.mjs expectedMembers).
DoorIds I hold (always 1 in peer.mjs).
Permanent cards on the table for me.
disturbance_in_the_force notices not yet shown.

validation.description: The local-state shape keeps exactly the canonical key set.
character.stats keeps vitality, world, matter, will.
cards keeps hand, deck_order_commitment, discard, archive and permanents_in_play.
region_peers keeps the strong / reachable tiers of sync_region_tiers.
